brief: A spending tracker where categories are geological layers — deeper is necessity, surface is discretionary

dominant_strengths: Strong conceptual metaphor: stratified earth-tone bands literally embody the geology=necessity mapping, making the brief instantly legible
Cohesive warm sediment palette with confident bold sans typography lends editorial weight and thematic unity
Layer labels (TOPSOIL, SUBSOIL, IGNEOUS, METAMORPHIC) reinforce the system creatively without feeling gimmicky
dominant_weaknesses: Severe text collision: category totals like '$1,240' overlap the layer label 'TOPSOIL', revealing broken z-order or grid math
Right-side Depth Analysis panel feels disconnected — the vertical slider lacks context, labels, and visual relationship to the strata
Emoji icons in rounded white tiles clash with the otherwise serious geological aesthetic, weakening craft and native feel
fix_priorities: Resolve overlapping totals vs. layer tags by reserving a dedicated right-margin column or moving stratum labels to the band edge
Replace emoji glyphs with custom monoline geological icons (pickaxe, strata, drill) for tonal consistency
Tie the Depth Analysis slider to actual layer positions with tick marks and labels so it reads as a cross-section, not decoration
Tighten vertical rhythm — sub-item chips feel floaty; align them to a baseline grid against the big totals
rationale.norman_balance: Strong visceral and reflective pull from the geological metaphor, but behavioral usability suffers from overlapping numbers and an ambiguous depth slider.
rationale.intent_fit: Yes — the stratified layer visualization directly and memorably executes the brief, though execution bugs undercut the concept.
